<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="top-gradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#top-gradient)"/>

  <!-- Key message bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="20" width="1200" height="60" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="20" width="6" height="60" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="60" y="56" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">
    <tspan>Lifetime depression risk is substantial — hundreds of millions affected worldwide each year</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="120" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Hundreds of Millions Affected</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- LEFT: 1 in 3 Women -->
  <rect x="40" y="150" width="560" height="280" rx="8" fill="#F0FDFA" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <use data-icon="users" x="270" y="170" width="48" height="48" fill="#00796B"/>
  <text x="295" y="270" text-anchor="middle" fill="#00796B" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="72" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>1 in 3</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="295" y="320" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Women</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="295" y="355" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>will experience major depression</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="295" y="380" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>in their lifetime</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- RIGHT: 1 in 5 Men -->
  <rect x="680" y="150" width="560" height="280" rx="8" fill="#F0FDFA" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <use data-icon="user" x="910" y="170" width="48" height="48" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="935" y="270" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="72" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>1 in 5</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="935" y="320" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Men</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="935" y="355" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>will experience major depression</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="935" y="380" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>in their lifetime</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Context text block -->
  <rect x="40" y="460" width="1200" height="150" rx="8" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="60" y="495" fill="#111827" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18">
    <tspan>Mental health conditions span from common disorders — depression and anxiety affect hundreds</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="520" fill="#111827" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18">
    <tspan>of millions each year — to less common but severe conditions like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="545" fill="#111827" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18">
    <tspan>that carry a large impact on individuals' lives.</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="580" fill="#00796B" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Poor mental health affects well-being, the ability to work, and relationships with family and community.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="660" x2="1240" y2="660" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="695" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">
    <tspan>Source: Our World in Data — Mental Health (Dattani, Rodés-Guirao, Ritchie, Roser, 2023); Data: IHME GBD 2025</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="640" y="695" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1220" y="695" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">02</text>
</svg>

  </text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="120" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="26" font-weight="bold">

  <use data-icon="comments" x="1026" y="206" width="48" height="48" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="1050" y="310" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Talking to Friends</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="1050" y="332" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>or Family</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="1050" y="372" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>A widely reported coping</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="1050" y="396" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>mechanism across diverse</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="1050" y="420" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>cultural contexts.</tspan>
  </text>
  <rect x="900" y="440" width="300" height="40" rx="6" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <text x="1050" y="466" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Cross-cultural</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Bottom takeaway -->
  <rect x="40" y="550" width="1200" height="60" rx="8" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="550" width="4" height="60" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <use data-icon="globe" x="60" y="562" width="36" height="36" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="110" y="586" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="top-gradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#top-gradient)"/>

  <!-- Key message bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="20" width="1200" height="60" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="20" width="6" height="60" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="60" y="56" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">
    <tspan>Five priorities for mental health policy — scaling interventions while maintaining specialized care</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="120" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="26" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Key Takeaways: Prioritizing Depression, Anxiety, and Closing the Treatment Gap</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- 5 numbered takeaway items -->
  <!-- Item 1 -->
  <rect x="40" y="155" width="1200" height="80" rx="8" fill="#F0FDFA" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="55" y="170" width="48" height="48" rx="24" fill="#00796B"/>
  <text x="79" y="202" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>1</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="190" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Depression + anxiety together represent the overwhelming majority of mental health DALYs</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="215" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>~694.6 and ~686.5 DALYs per 100K respectively — combined ~80% of total burden</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Item 2 -->
  <rect x="40" y="250" width="1200" height="80" rx="8" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="55" y="265" width="48" height="48" rx="24" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <text x="79" y="297" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>2</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="285" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Schizophrenia + bipolar carry disproportionate individual burden</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="310" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>Schizophrenia: 210.2 DALYs/100K — severe disability despite lower population prevalence</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Item 3 -->
  <rect x="40" y="345" width="1200" height="80" rx="8" fill="#F0FDFA" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="55" y="360" width="48" height="48" rx="24" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="79" y="392" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>3</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="380" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Treatment exists but access and quality remain inadequate</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="405" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>Especially in low- and middle-income countries — effective treatments are available but not reaching those in need</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Item 4 -->
  <rect x="40" y="440" width="1200" height="80" rx="8" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <rect x="55" y="455" width="48" height="48" rx="24" fill="#C62828"/>
  <text x="79" y="487" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>4</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="475" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Stigma suppresses both help-seeking and accurate data</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="500" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16">
    <tspan>Underreporting means the true burden is likely higher than current estimates suggest</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Item 5 -->
  <rect x="40" y="535" width="1200" height="80" rx="8" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="535" width="4" height="80" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <rect x="55" y="550" width="48" height="48" rx="24" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="79" y="582" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0D1117" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>5</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="570" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>Policy should prioritize scaling evidence-based interventions for common disorders</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="595" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">
    <tspan>while maintaining specialized care for severe conditions like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="660" x2="1240" y2="660" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="695" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">
    <tspan>Source: Our World in Data — Mental Health (Dattani, Rodés-Guirao, Ritchie, Roser, 2023); Data: IHME GBD 2025</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="640" y="695" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1220" y="695" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">08</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this briefing on the global burden of mental illness. Today we will walk through the latest data from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation — published through Our World in Data — covering prevalence, disease burden measured in DALYs, and the persistent treatment gap that policy must address. [Pause]

Key points: ① Framing the scope — global data, 2023 ② Source credibility — IHME GBD ③ Audience orientation — policy analysts and program planners
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_prevalence_scale

[Transition] Let us begin with the sheer scale of the problem.

The lifetime risk of major depression is striking: roughly one in three women and one in five men will experience it. [Pause] That is not a rare condition — it is a defining public health challenge. Mental health conditions range from these very common disorders to less common but highly disabling ones like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Hundreds of millions are affected each year, with consequences for employment, relationships, and community well-being.

Key points: ① 1 in 3 women, 1 in 5 men — lifetime depression risk ② Spectrum from common to severe ③ Broad societal impact
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_burden_by_category

[Transition] Now let us quantify that burden using a standardized measure: disability-adjusted life years.

This chart is the core of today's briefing. [Data] Depressive disorders generate roughly 695 DALYs per 100,000 people, and anxiety disorders are virtually identical at about 687. Together, they account for approximately 80 percent of the total mental health disease burden across these five categories. [Pause] Schizophrenia contributes 210 DALYs — a distant third but still substantial. Bipolar disorder and eating disorders round out the picture at 95 and 48 DALYs respectively.

Key points: ① Depression and anxiety dominate ② Combined ~80% of burden ③ Schizophrenia third but significant
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_depression_vs_anxiety

[Transition] Let us zoom in on that remarkable near-parity between the top two conditions.

The difference between depressive and anxiety disorders is just 8 DALYs per 100,000 — essentially a rounding error at global scale. [Pause] This matters for policy because anxiety disorders have historically received less attention and funding than depression, despite carrying a virtually identical population-level burden. Combined, these two conditions generate roughly 1,381 DALYs per 100,000 — underscoring why they must be the primary target of any scaled mental health intervention.

Key points: ① Near-equal burden — only 8.1 DALYs apart ② Anxiety historically underfunded relative to its impact ③ Both deserve equal policy prioritization
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_severe_conditions

[Transition] While common disorders dominate the aggregate numbers, we must not lose sight of severe conditions.

[Data] Schizophrenia at 210 DALYs per 100,000 is roughly a third of depression's burden at the population level — but per individual affected, the disability is profound. People with schizophrenia face chronic, often lifelong impairment requiring sustained clinical support. Bipolar disorder contributes about 95 DALYs, with episodic disability that demands ongoing management. [Pause] The policy implication is clear: while we scale interventions for depression and anxiety, we must maintain and strengthen specialized care pathways for these severe conditions.

Key points: ① Schizophrenia — 210.2 DALYs, severe per-case disability ② Bipolar — 94.6 DALYs, episodic but meaningful ③ Policy must balance scale and specialization
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_treatment_gap

[Transition] Given the burden we have just reviewed, you might expect treatment systems to be well-matched. They are not.

Four barriers drive the treatment gap. First, stigma — many people simply will not disclose symptoms, not even to a doctor. Second, access — in low- and middle-income countries, mental health services are severely under-resourced. Third, quality — even where treatment exists, it often falls short. And fourth, underreporting — because people avoid disclosing, our prevalence estimates are likely conservative. [Pause] The true global burden of mental illness is almost certainly higher than what the data shows.

Key points: ① Stigma prevents disclosure ② Access gaps especially in LMICs ③ Quality deficiencies ④ Underreporting masks true scale
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_coping_strategies

[Transition] In the absence of adequate treatment, people find their own ways to cope.

Global survey data reveals three dominant strategies. In higher-income settings, prescribed medication is the most common response. In many regions worldwide, religious and spiritual activities serve as the primary coping mechanism. And across nearly all cultures, talking to friends and family remains a widely reported source of support. [Pause] This diversity has a direct policy implication: interventions must be culturally sensitive. A medication-first approach that works in one setting may be ineffective or even counterproductive in another.

Key points: ① Medication — higher-income settings ② Religious/spiritual — globally prevalent ③ Social support — cross-cultural ④ No one-size-fits-all policy
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_key_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five priorities for mental health policy.

First, depression and anxiety together account for the overwhelming majority of the disease burden — they must be the primary targets. Second, schizophrenia and bipolar carry disproportionate individual burden and cannot be neglected. Third, effective treatments exist but are not reaching those who need them. Fourth, stigma remains the silent barrier — it suppresses both help-seeking and the data we rely on for planning. [Pause] And fifth — the actionable synthesis — policy should prioritize scaling evidence-based interventions for common disorders while maintaining specialized care for severe conditions. Thank you.

Key points: ① Depression + anxiety = dominant burden ② Severe conditions need specialized care ③ Treatment gap must close ④ Stigma reduction is foundational ⑤ Scale common, specialize severe
Duration: 2 minutes

# 01_cover

Welcome to this briefing on the global burden of mental illness. Today we will walk through the latest data from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation — published through Our World in Data — covering prevalence, disease burden measured in DALYs, and the persistent treatment gap that policy must address. [Pause]

Key points: ① Framing the scope — global data, 2023 ② Source credibility — IHME GBD ③ Audience orientation — policy analysts and program planners
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_prevalence_scale

[Transition] Let us begin with the sheer scale of the problem.

The lifetime risk of major depression is striking: roughly one in three women and one in five men will experience it. [Pause] That is not a rare condition — it is a defining public health challenge. Mental health conditions range from these very common disorders to less common but highly disabling ones like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Hundreds of millions are affected each year, with consequences for employment, relationships, and community well-being.

Key points: ① 1 in 3 women, 1 in 5 men — lifetime depression risk ② Spectrum from common to severe ③ Broad societal impact
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_burden_by_category

[Transition] Now let us quantify that burden using a standardized measure: disability-adjusted life years.

This chart is the core of today's briefing. [Data] Depressive disorders generate roughly 695 DALYs per 100,000 people, and anxiety disorders are virtually identical at about 687. Together, they account for approximately 80 percent of the total mental health disease burden across these five categories. [Pause] Schizophrenia contributes 210 DALYs — a distant third but still substantial. Bipolar disorder and eating disorders round out the picture at 95 and 48 DALYs respectively.

Key points: ① Depression and anxiety dominate ② Combined ~80% of burden ③ Schizophrenia third but significant
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_depression_vs_anxiety

[Transition] Let us zoom in on that remarkable near-parity between the top two conditions.

The difference between depressive and anxiety disorders is just 8 DALYs per 100,000 — essentially a rounding error at global scale. [Pause] This matters for policy because anxiety disorders have historically received less attention and funding than depression, despite carrying a virtually identical population-level burden. Combined, these two conditions generate roughly 1,381 DALYs per 100,000 — underscoring why they must be the primary target of any scaled mental health intervention.

Key points: ① Near-equal burden — only 8.1 DALYs apart ② Anxiety historically underfunded relative to its impact ③ Both deserve equal policy prioritization
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_severe_conditions

[Transition] While common disorders dominate the aggregate numbers, we must not lose sight of severe conditions.

[Data] Schizophrenia at 210 DALYs per 100,000 is roughly a third of depression's burden at the population level — but per individual affected, the disability is profound. People with schizophrenia face chronic, often lifelong impairment requiring sustained clinical support. Bipolar disorder contributes about 95 DALYs, with episodic disability that demands ongoing management. [Pause] The policy implication is clear: while we scale interventions for depression and anxiety, we must maintain and strengthen specialized care pathways for these severe conditions.

Key points: ① Schizophrenia — 210.2 DALYs, severe per-case disability ② Bipolar — 94.6 DALYs, episodic but meaningful ③ Policy must balance scale and specialization
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_treatment_gap

[Transition] Given the burden we have just reviewed, you might expect treatment systems to be well-matched. They are not.

Four barriers drive the treatment gap. First, stigma — many people simply will not disclose symptoms, not even to a doctor. Second, access — in low- and middle-income countries, mental health services are severely under-resourced. Third, quality — even where treatment exists, it often falls short. And fourth, underreporting — because people avoid disclosing, our prevalence estimates are likely conservative. [Pause] The true global burden of mental illness is almost certainly higher than what the data shows.

Key points: ① Stigma prevents disclosure ② Access gaps especially in LMICs ③ Quality deficiencies ④ Underreporting masks true scale
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_coping_strategies

[Transition] In the absence of adequate treatment, people find their own ways to cope.

Global survey data reveals three dominant strategies. In higher-income settings, prescribed medication is the most common response. In many regions worldwide, religious and spiritual activities serve as the primary coping mechanism. And across nearly all cultures, talking to friends and family remains a widely reported source of support. [Pause] This diversity has a direct policy implication: interventions must be culturally sensitive. A medication-first approach that works in one setting may be ineffective or even counterproductive in another.

Key points: ① Medication — higher-income settings ② Religious/spiritual — globally prevalent ③ Social support — cross-cultural ④ No one-size-fits-all policy
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_key_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five priorities for mental health policy.

First, depression and anxiety together account for the overwhelming majority of the disease burden — they must be the primary targets. Second, schizophrenia and bipolar carry disproportionate individual burden and cannot be neglected. Third, effective treatments exist but are not reaching those who need them. Fourth, stigma remains the silent barrier — it suppresses both help-seeking and the data we rely on for planning. [Pause] And fifth — the actionable synthesis — policy should prioritize scaling evidence-based interventions for common disorders while maintaining specialized care for severe conditions. Thank you.

Key points: ① Depression + anxiety = dominant burden ② Severe conditions need specialized care ③ Treatment gap must close ④ Stigma reduction is foundational ⑤ Scale common, specialize severe
Duration: 2 minutes
